examples.solution_text:
Increase the power to $5$ and divide by $(-3)\times5$.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\int(6-3x)^4\,dx\\&=\frac{(6-3x)^5}{(-3)\times5}+C\\&=-\frac{(6-3x)^5}{15}+C\end{aligned}$

Retain the outside factor $8$, increase the power to $4$ and divide by $3\times4$.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\int8(3x-2)^3\,dx\\&=\frac{8(3x-2)^4}{3\times4}+C\\&=\frac{2(3x-2)^4}{3}+C\end{aligned}$

Write the square root as a fractional power.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\int\sqrt{8-3x}\,dx\\&=\int(8-3x)^{\frac12}\,dx\\&=\frac{(8-3x)^{\frac32}}{(-3)\times\frac32}+C\\&=-\frac{2(8-3x)^{\frac32}}{9}+C\end{aligned}$

Write the reciprocal using a negative power.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\int\frac{10}{(7-2x)^4}\,dx\\&=\int10(7-2x)^{-4}\,dx\\&=\frac{10(7-2x)^{-3}}{(-2)\times(-3)}+C\\&=\frac{5}{3(7-2x)^3}+C\end{aligned}$

The integrand is a polynomial, so it is continuous on $[0,1]$.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\int_0^1 2(2x+3)^2\,dx\\&=\left[\frac{2(2x+3)^3}{2\times3}\right]_0^1\\&=\frac{5^3}{3}-\frac{3^3}{3}\\&=\frac{125-27}{3}\\&=\frac{98}{3}\end{aligned}$

examples.derivation: The new power is 5 and the inner derivative is -3, giving -(6-3x)^5/15+C. Differentiating gives (-1/15)·5·(-3)(6-3x)^4=(6-3x)^4.
Rewrite the root as (8-3x)^(1/2). Dividing by (-3)(3/2) gives -2(8-3x)^(3/2)/9+C. Differentiation yields (8-3x)^(1/2) on the real-domain interior.
Rewrite as 10(7-2x)^(-4). The primitive is 10(7-2x)^(-3)/[(-2)(-3)]+C=5/[3(7-2x)^3]+C. Differentiating gives 10(7-2x)^(-4), for x≠7/2.
The chain rule gives y'=5·4(4x+3)^4=20(4x+3)^4. Reversing this derivative gives the general primitive (4x+3)^5+C.
The polynomial integrand is continuous on [0,1]. A primitive is (2x+3)^3/3, whose derivative is 2(2x+3)^2. Endpoint subtraction gives (5^3-3^3)/3=98/3.
